prompt.context_jp: 静まり返った会議室の空気___、鉛のように重かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 静まり返った会議室の空気___、鉛のように重かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Opening narration — pick the particle that marks the air of the room as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: This is a descriptive, scene-setting line: the narrator takes 会議室の空気 as the topic and tells us something about it (heavy as lead). は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the air as brand-new information at the moment of noticing, which doesn't fit a calm narrative description. を is wrong because 重い is an adjective, not a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: The air (topic) was heavy. — describing a known scene.
The air became heavy. — reports a change as new info.

prompt.context_jp: だからこそ、あの叱責のあとにけろりとしている鷹野の顔つき___、ますます気になった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鷹野の顔つき___、ますます気になった。
prompt.prompt_en: Hiwada notices something that bothers him — pick the particle that marks what caught his attention.

feedback.correct_en: 気になる takes が for the thing that strikes you. Takano's expression newly catches his attention here, so が fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 顔つき a topic being described, which clashes with the ‘newly bothering me’ feel. に would mark a target of some other verb, not the subject of 気になる.

contrast_examples.en: The expression catches my attention.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔つきは変わっていない。
contrast_examples.en: The expression (topic) hasn't changed.

prompt.context_jp: 数日後の営業部では、雉谷___満面の笑みでカレンダーを掲げていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 雉谷___満面の笑みでカレンダーを掲げていた。
prompt.prompt_en: A new scene opens and we see who is doing something — pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a scene-introducing sentence — the camera pans in and we newly see Kijitani doing something. New-information が is right.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Kijitani is already the running topic, but the scene has just shifted. で here would wrongly treat 雉谷 as a location/means.

contrast_examples.en: Kijitani was smiling. — new info, first notice.

contrast_examples.jp: 雉谷は毎日笑っている。
contrast_examples.en: Kijitani (as topic) smiles every day.

prompt.context_jp: ざわめきが一段落したあとも、鶸田だけ___席に戻れずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鶸田だけ___席に戻れずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Everyone else returned to their seats; pick the particle after 鶸田だけ.

feedback.correct_en: だけは explicitly contrasts Hiwada against everyone else who did go back. Contrastive は is the natural partner for だけ here.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would exhaustively identify ‘the one who couldn't,’ but the sentence's feel is contrast with the rest, not a quiz-style identification. を doesn't fit this intransitive clause.

contrast_examples.en: Only he (unlike the others) didn't come.
He is the only one who knows. — exhaustive identification.

prompt.context_jp: スマートフォンの通知音___、静かな部屋に小さな波紋を投げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: スマートフォンの通知音___、静かな部屋に小さな波紋を投げた。
prompt.prompt_en: A quiet room — then suddenly something happens. Which particle introduces this?

feedback.correct_en: The notification sound suddenly intrudes on the silence — it's a new event bursting into the scene. が marks this fresh event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would set up the sound as an ongoing topic, flattening the sudden-event feel. で (location/means) doesn't fit the subject slot of 投げた.

contrast_examples.en: A notification sounded. — sudden event.
Notification sounds (as a topic) are annoying.

prompt.context_jp: 妻の不倫という疑念___、確信でもなければ幻でもなく、ちょうど中庸のあたりで彼の胸を締め付け続けた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妻の不倫という疑念___、確信でもなければ幻でもなく…
prompt.prompt_en: The sentence then characterizes the suspicion. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence takes 疑念 as its topic and then describes its nature (neither certainty nor illusion). This classic ‘A は X でも Y でもない’ frame uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn the suspicion into newly observed info, which doesn't match this reflective description. に marks targets/times, not topics.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は学生でも社会人でもない。
contrast_examples.en: He is neither student nor working adult. — descriptive topic frame.
A suspicion arose. — new event.

prompt.context_jp: ただし、その衝動を口に出したの___、鶸田ではなく、いつの間にか彼のそばに立っていた鳩山だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その衝動を口に出したの___、鶸田ではなく、…鳩山だった。
prompt.prompt_en: A ‘not X but Y’ identifying sentence — pick the particle after 口に出したの.

feedback.correct_en: This is the cleft pattern 〜のは Yだ (‘the one who did X was Y’), used here with a contrast (not Hiwada, but Hatoyama). は is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが could mark a subject noun clause, but the sentence ends with 鳩山だった — a predicate nominal explaining ‘the one who…’, which requires のは. を wouldn't fit at all.

contrast_examples.en: The one who called is me.
I called. — plain new-info subject.

prompt.context_jp: だが、笑いが止むと、朱雀の眉間にはうっすらと皺___寄っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朱雀の眉間にはうっすらと皺___寄っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: After the laughter, we notice a new detail on Suzaku's face. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic ‘A には B がある/寄る’ pattern: the location is topicalized with は, and the newly-noticed thing (the wrinkle) is introduced with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は on 皺 would double-topic awkwardly, since 眉間には is already the topic. を doesn't work with the intransitive 寄る.

contrast_examples.en: On the desk there is a book.
The book is on the desk. — different topic choice.

prompt.context_jp: いつもより一時間早く出社した鳩山___、まだ人の少ないオフィスに一番乗りで足を踏み入れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつもより一時間早く出社した鳩山___、まだ人の少ないオフィスに…足を踏み入れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Hatoyama is the ongoing character of this paragraph. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Hatoyama is already the main character and the modifying clause (一時間早く出社した) is simply more info about him. Topic は keeps him as the running theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Hatoyama as newly introduced, but we've been following him for several paragraphs. を can't mark the actor of 踏み入れた.

contrast_examples.en: Hatoyama (topic) came in early.
Someone came in early. — new info.

prompt.context_jp: 鷹野に連れられて向かった先___、社内で「変人の集い」と噂される鵙尾たちの島だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鷹野に連れられて向かった先___、…鵙尾たちの島だった。
prompt.prompt_en: An ‘A は B だった’ identifying sentence. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence takes ‘the place they headed to’ as the topic and tells us what it was. The ‘A は B だった’ frame requires は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would weirdly present the place as new info in an identification equation. で would mark a location of some other action, not the predicate.

contrast_examples.en: The place we arrived was the station.
A station came into view. — new info.

prompt.context_jp: 妻の帰り___遅い日は、今月に入ってから数え切れなくなっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妻の帰り___遅い日は…
prompt.prompt_en: Inside the relative clause ‘days when the wife's return is late.’ Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/modifying clause, subject marking defaults to が: 帰りが遅い modifies 日. は is usually blocked here because it belongs to the main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this noun-modifying clause would compete with the main topic 日は and sound unnatural. を doesn't work with the adjective 遅い.

contrast_examples.en: A person whose height is tall. — が inside modifier.
This person is tall. — main topic は, embedded が.

prompt.context_jp: 朱雀部長の前___、鷹野は深く頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朱雀部長の前___、鷹野は深く頭を下げていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking where Takano is bowing.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place. The bowing (頭を下げる) is an action performed in front of the director.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination (‘toward the front of…’), which sounds odd for a static bow. を would require a transitive verb that takes 前 as its object.

contrast_examples.en: I apologized in front of the director. — で: action location.
Go to the station. — に: destination.

prompt.context_jp: 一か月が過ぎるころ、鳩山___目に見えて変わっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鳩山___目に見えて変わっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: A reflective statement about Hatoyama after a month. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Hatoyama has been the ongoing character; the narrator is now reflecting on him as the topic and describing a visible change. Topic は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Hatoyama as newly spotted, which contradicts the ‘by now, after a month’ summarizing feel. も would wrongly imply ‘Hatoyama too.’

contrast_examples.en: He (as topic) has changed.
He has changed! — exclamatory new realization.

prompt.context_jp: 「鳩山さん___会社の良心です 辞められたら みんな困ります！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 鳩山さん___会社の良心です。
prompt.prompt_en: An ‘A is B’ characterization. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Standard ‘A は B です’ frame: ‘Hatoyama is the conscience of the company.’ The speaker is describing a known person.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it an identifying ‘it is Hatoyama who is the conscience’ (answering a question), but no such question is being answered. を doesn't fit the copula.

contrast_examples.en: Hatoyama is the conscience. — description.
It's Hatoyama who is the conscience. — exhaustive answer.

prompt.context_jp: こうして始まった鳩山の「普通脱出計画」は、鷹野の付き添いのもとで、日を追うごとに___を増していった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 日を追うごとに___を増していった。
prompt.prompt_en: The plan gets more and more ___ as days go by. Pick the word.

feedback.correct_en: The whole point of the ‘escape ordinariness’ plan is to grow more outlandish. 突飛さ (outlandishness) is the exact word the story uses here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 普通さ contradicts the plan's goal (to leave ordinariness). 真面目さ (seriousness) describes Hatoyama's old self, not the increasing wildness of the activities.

contrast_examples.en: an outlandish action
an ordinary action

prompt.context_jp: 「いよいよ ___の納め時か～」
prompt.prompt_jp: いよいよ ___の納め時か～
prompt.prompt_en: A set phrase a bachelor says when he finally gets married (‘time to pay up’).

feedback.correct_en: 年貢の納め時 is a fixed idiom meaning ‘the time has finally come to settle up’ — classically used, half-jokingly, when a bachelor marries.
feedback.incorrect_en: 税金 and 家賃 are real payments, but the idiom only works with the historical 年貢 (feudal rice tax). Swapping the noun breaks the set phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: とうとう年貢の納め時だ。
contrast_examples.en: At last, time to settle up.
It's time to pay taxes. — literal, not the idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 「余計なことを考えるな 大体 美沙が 不倫なんて する___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 美沙が 不倫なんて する___
prompt.prompt_en: Hatoyama talks himself down. Pick the ending that means ‘there's no way she would do that.’

feedback.correct_en: 〜するわけない means ‘there's no way X would happen’ — Hatoyama is firmly denying the possibility of her cheating.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜することない means ‘there's no need to do X,’ a totally different meaning. 〜ところない is not a natural pattern.

contrast_examples.en: There's no way he'd get angry.
There's no need to apologize.

prompt.context_jp: ___も積もれば山となるという言葉があるように、鶸田の目にも、その小さな挑戦が確実に何かを鳩山の中に堆積させていくのが見て取れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___も積もれば山となる
prompt.prompt_en: A famous proverb about small things building up. Fill the blank.

feedback.correct_en: The fixed proverb is 塵も積もれば山となる — ‘even dust, piled up, becomes a mountain.’ The narrator uses it twice in this chapter to frame Hatoyama's gradual change.
feedback.incorrect_en: 砂 (sand) and 雪 (snow) feel plausibly tiny, but the idiom is locked to 塵. Other words make it merely a literal observation, not the proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.
The snow piles up. — literal, not idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 真面目に上司に仕える者ほど、些細な叱責を___ものだと、彼は入社してからようやく理解するようになっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 些細な叱責を___ものだ
prompt.prompt_en: Earnest employees tend to ___ even small scoldings (= keep dwelling on them).

feedback.correct_en: 〜を引きずる literally ‘to drag along,’ idiomatically means to keep carrying a bad feeling or past event with you. Perfect for ‘can't let a scolding go.’
feedback.incorrect_en: 引き受ける means ‘to accept/take on (a task),’ which doesn't fit lingering emotions. 引き出す means ‘to draw out/withdraw,’ also unrelated.

contrast_examples.en: To keep dwelling on a breakup.
To take on responsibility.

prompt.context_jp: ギャル:「ウチの店 敬語禁止だから」。鷹野が最初に言ったのは「よろしくお願いします」でした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 敬語禁止のギャルカフェで、鷹野の挨拶として自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: The gal café bans polite speech. Which greeting fits the café's casual rule?

choices.text: よろしくお願いいたします
よろしくお願いします

feedback.correct_en: The staff explicitly ban 敬語, so the casual よろしくね matches the house rule. In the story, Takano's polite version is exactly what the gal calls out as against the rules.
feedback.incorrect_en: よろしくお願いします and the even more formal いたします are 敬語 — exactly what the café forbids. That's why the gal says ‘敬語禁止！’ to Takano.

contrast_examples.en: Nice to meet ya! — casual.

contrast_examples.jp: よろしくお願いいたします。
contrast_examples.en: Pleased to make your acquaintance. — very polite / 敬語.

prompt.context_jp: 妻が、冒険できない夫に半ばあきれて言う一言。
prompt.prompt_jp: 妻のセリフとして、ドラマの文脈で自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as the wife's half-exasperated jab?

choices.text: あなたって ホント 普通よね
あなたって ホント 普通ですよね
あなたって とても 普通です

feedback.correct_en: Between a married couple at home, the casual sentence-final よね plus the mildly feminine よね lands exactly as the show plays it: a sigh of ‘you really are just plain.’
feedback.incorrect_en: です・ですよね makes a wife sound oddly formal to her husband at home. Option C is grammatical but flat and lacks the exasperation.

contrast_examples.en: You really are plain, aren't you. — casual, intimate.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんは普通ですね。
contrast_examples.en: Mr. Tanaka is ordinary, isn't he. — polite distance.

prompt.context_jp: 「ヤンキーだったこと 自分の人生に___ メリットないなって思ったんで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の人生に___ メリットない
prompt.prompt_en: Karasumori stresses ‘not even the slightest benefit.’ Pick the phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 1ミリも〜ない is a very common casual intensifier meaning ‘not even a millimeter / not in the slightest.’ Fits Karasumori's blunt tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 1キロも or 1トンも imply large quantities, which is the opposite of the ‘not even a tiny bit’ nuance. These simply don't form the idiom.

contrast_examples.en: I don't have the slightest interest.
I gained a kilo. — literal measurement.

prompt.context_jp: プロンプトを打ち込む彼女の指___、依頼というより、新しい遊びを企てるような軽やかさを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の指___、…軽やかさを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narrator describes Takano's fingers. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A literary descriptive sentence: ‘her fingers (topic) had a lightness about them.’ The narrator sets 指 as the theme and describes it. は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the fingers as a newly noticed subject in an exclamation, but the sentence is a reflective description. を doesn't fit 帯びる's subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: His eyes (topic) were gentle.
His eyes suddenly flashed. — new event.

prompt.context_jp: 夜明け前の空気は冷たく、寝間着のままベランダ___出て、彼はただ深く息を吐いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ベランダ___出て、…
prompt.prompt_en: He steps out onto the balcony. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に出る marks the goal of the movement — he moves outward and arrives on the balcony. に is the right directional particle here.
feedback.incorrect_en: ベランダで出る would wrongly treat the balcony as the location of some action. ベランダを出る means ‘exit the balcony,’ i.e. leave it — the opposite of what he does.

contrast_examples.en: Go out (to the outside).
Leave the house.

prompt.context_jp: 「今日も展示会の準備だから 会場近くのホテルに___ね モモのごはん お願い」
prompt.prompt_jp: 会場近くのホテルに___ね
prompt.prompt_en: The wife tells Hatoyama she's staying overnight at a hotel near the venue.

feedback.correct_en: 泊まる means to stay overnight (at a hotel, friend's place, etc.) — exactly the business-trip situation and the chapter's title (泊まりの続く夜).
feedback.incorrect_en: 住む means to live/reside long-term, not a one-night stay. 止まる (same reading as 泊まる) means to come to a stop and is a different verb entirely.

contrast_examples.en: Stay at a hotel overnight.
Live in Tokyo.

prompt.context_jp: 週末、久しぶりに家に戻ってきた妻___、鳩山の前に見慣れない柄のシャツを掲げてみせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 久しぶりに家に戻ってきた妻___、…シャツを掲げてみせた。
prompt.prompt_en: The wife is reintroduced after being away. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The wife is a known character the chapter keeps returning to; the narrator uses her as the topic of this scene (‘as for his wife, she held up…’). は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame her as newly spotted, but she's a familiar character the reader has already met. も (‘too’) has no sense in context.

contrast_examples.en: His wife (topic) came home.
His wife has come home! — exclamatory news.
